This is the operational library behind ManasFlow: 11 workflow automations across 4 categories that we actually run for clients and on our own business, each shown as a step flow with a link to the full breakdown and a template on ManasN8N, our own workflow automation platform.

How we standardize engineering work as reusable Claude Code skills, so every build starts from a proven playbook instead of a blank prompt.

AI Product Build: From Idea to Production
Our end-to-end process for shipping an AI product or feature: scope the risky part first, build on proven rails, launch with evals and guardrails.
3-8 weeks: one week to de-risk the AI core, the rest is shell, guardrails, and rollout
n8n Workflow Builder: Custom, Production-Ready Builds
We build custom n8n workflows for your business that survive production: mapped processes, idempotent builds, Slack alerts, and a clean handover.

Lead Qualification Workflow: HubSpot and Salesforce Scoring
Lead qualification that captures, scores and routes inbound leads in HubSpot or Salesforce, so hot leads get a booking link in minutes and cold ones wait.

Customer Support Automation
Automate support the safe way: triage everything, draft replies for human review first, deflect FAQs with grounded answers only, and earn autonomy with data.
3-6 weeks to reach reviewed drafts in production; autonomy decisions come after real usage data, not on a launch date
Automated Content Adaptation Workflows (GEO + SEO)
Our automated content adaptation workflow for GEO and SEO: real search data drives research, human review gates every draft, schema and links ship by default.
2-4 weeks to install the system; rankings compound over months, and anyone promising faster is selling something
GTM Automation Workflow: The Six-Step Outbound Stack
The six-step GTM automation stack we build: find people, spot buying signals, identify visitors, reach out, log in the CRM, feed content back.
3-5 weeks to a working pipeline; expect another few weeks of approval-queue feedback before draft quality settles
AI Agent Deployment
How we take an agent from working-on-a-laptop to production: scoped permissions, real secrets handling, sandboxing, eval gates, observability, and rollback.
2-6 weeks depending on how many systems the agent touches and the state of the existing code
Signal-Based Outbound: From Buying Signal to First Line
A buying signal becomes a verified contact, a message that opens with what just happened, and a reply logged in your CRM. Signal, Clay, Instantly, CRM.
3-5 weeks to the first live sequence, mostly set by sending domain warm-up
Website Visitor Outreach Workflow: Same-Day, Page-Specific
Identify the companies reading your pricing page, score them against your ICP, and send a same-day message that references the page they viewed.
2-4 weeks once the identification tool is installed; longer if new sending domains need to warm up
CRM Hygiene Automation: The Weekly Job That Keeps It Clean
A weekly n8n job for HubSpot, Salesforce or Zoho: merge duplicates, flag stalled deals, route new leads and send one owner a Slack digest.
1-3 weeks depending on the CRM and how much existing duplication needs a first cleanup

Workflow automation is software that runs a repeatable business process end to end (capture, enrich, decide, act) without a person doing each step by hand. The best workflow automations still keep a human checkpoint on anything outward-facing, like a send or a customer reply, so speed does not come at the cost of a mistake reaching a customer.

Start with the process that is high-frequency, well-understood, and has a clear failure mode you can design for, like lead qualification, support triage, or an n8n pipeline that already runs manually today. The 8 workflows on this page are the ones we actually run, each with the real steps, tools, and honest timeline instead of a generic template.

Real. Every entry here is a process ManasFlow runs for clients or on its own business, documented on its own detail page with the real steps, tools, deliverables, and cases where we would tell you not to use it. Nothing on this page is a hypothetical or a stock diagram.
